questions.q: What is impact analysis, in CMDB terms?
options: Guessing which applications might be affected based on experience
Starting at a failed CI and walking its real relationship graph outward to see what actually depends on it
A report that lists every CI in the CMDB alphabetically
A manual survey sent to application owners after an outage
questions.explain: Impact analysis uses the exact relationship mechanism from Lessons 5 and 6 — it's a graph walk starting from the failed CI.

questions.q: Why is checking only the CIs directly related to a failed CI usually not enough?
options: Direct relationships are always wrong and should be ignored
Real impact often sits multiple hops away — the full chain through transitive relationships, not just the first hop, reaches the business services people actually notice
ServiceNow only stores one level of relationship per CI
Direct relationships are only used for Discovery, never for impact analysis
questions.explain: Transitive impact means following relationships through multiple hops until reaching the applications and business services that actually matter.

questions.q: In the worked example, what is the honest answer to "what's affected if this database goes down," once the full relationship chain is followed?
options: Nothing — database servers have no dependents
Only the one application server directly connected to it
The Online Ordering business service, and everyone who relies on placing orders through it
Every CI in the entire CMDB
questions.explain: Following the chain from database server to application server to application to business service gives the level of impact a stakeholder actually needs to hear.

questions.q: Why do Change Risk Assessment and CAB Conflict Detection, built in a later course, actually depend on this lesson's relationship work?
options: They don't depend on relationship data at all; they use separate, independent calculations
Both features run the same underlying impact-analysis graph walk, so missing or backward relationships make them confidently miscalculate risk or silently miss real conflicts
They only check the CI's name field, not its relationships
They replace the need for accurate relationship data entirely
questions.explain: Both features ask questions like "does this touch a business-critical CI" or "does this affect the same CI as another change" — both are impact-analysis queries underneath.

questions.q: What's the real danger of running impact analysis on missing or backward relationship data?
options: The query simply fails with an error every time
It produces a confident, wrong answer that people may act on — worse than having no answer at all
There is no danger; impact analysis always self-corrects
ServiceNow prevents impact analysis from running unless relationships are perfect
questions.explain: Impact analysis built on bad relationship data doesn't fail loudly — it returns a wrong answer that looks trustworthy.
